records.recommendation: The EIA-860M table for August 2026 has plant code 1077, Sutherland, in Marshall County, 0.3 km from GEM's coordinates. Its generator 1 (37.5 MW) and generator 3 (81.6 MW) are retired natural gas steam turbines from 1955 and 1961, both retired in 2017. Bobcat is a new 720 MW combustion turbine plant built next to the Marshalltown Generating Station, which is EIA plant 1068 and plant 58236. So Sutherland is the nearby retired plant and not this project. I would not link Bobcat to plant 1077 or to its generators. Please check whether a retired Sutherland record exists in GEM.
records.researcher_notes: I found no document that says Bobcat is on the former Sutherland site. Alliant says only that it is next to Marshalltown Generating Station.

records.recommendation: GEM's start year is 2021. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 gives 1968, which is when the original coal unit started. For a conversion, GEM wants the year the unit began burning gas. The Environmental Protection Agency letter from March 2022 says the conversion would be done by January 1, 2022. A 2022 news report in GEM's sources said it was nearly done in May 2022, and EIA still showed coal in October 2022. So 2021 looks too early and 2022 or later looks likelier. I could not find a document that gives the exact date. Please keep 2021 only if you have a source for it.

records.recommendation: Keep the placeholder for now and ask the reviewer whether the 430 MW combined cycle unit is still planned. If not, the placeholder could be cancelled.
records.researcher_notes: This placeholder holds the 430 MW combined cycle unit for 2029 that Interstate Power and Light modeled in its Resource Evaluation Study. I could not read the study itself, because it is filed with the Iowa Utilities Commission in docket RPU-2021-0003 and I did not reach that filing system. Comments filed by Synapse Energy Economics on April 7, 2025 describe the study, which is dated February 13, 2025. They say the main flat load portfolio adds over 1,500 MW of new gas, made up of a 430 MW combined cycle unit and the rest peaking units. They also say the company expected combined cycle units to be available no earlier than 2029. Alliant Energy's quarterly report for June 30, 2026 lists only simple-cycle gas projects: about 720 MW in Linn County (Morgan Valley) and about 1,200 MW near Emery Station (Riverhawk). It does not mention a combined cycle unit at all. Bobcat (720 MW) is already tracked as its own plant. I found no source that says the 430 MW combined cycle unit was dropped or replaced, and none that says it is still planned. So the placeholder cannot be confirmed or removed on the evidence found. A reviewer should check the docket or ask Alliant.

records.recommendation: No change needed. All seven MidAmerican placeholders match the plan. Optionally set this one to 233 MW to match the plan's rounded size.
records.researcher_notes: MidAmerican's Resource Evaluation Study of November 1, 2024 has a Preferred Portfolio table of gas combustion turbine additions. It lists 233 MW in 2028, 233 MW in 2029, 233 MW in 2031, 233 MW in 2033, 233 MW in 2035, 699 MW in 2041, 466 MW in 2042, 466 MW in 2043 and 699 MW in 2044, for a total of 3,495 MW. The 2028 and 2029 entries are the Orient Energy Center. The other seven are the placeholders: 233 MW in 2031 (this plant, which GEM holds at 232.5 MW), 233 MW in 2033, 233 MW in 2035, 699 MW in 2041, 466 MW in 2042, 466 MW in 2043 and 699 MW in 2044. Every year and size matches GEM, except that this plant is 232.5 MW in GEM and 233 MW in the plan. The plan models turbines in 233 MW blocks, and Orient's two turbines are each 232.5 MW, so the 0.5 MW gap is rounding. I read the table in the downloaded plan text.

records.recommendation: Leave both units at 2028. The plan's 2029 entry for the second turbine is older than the company's own later statements.
records.researcher_notes: The tab note says MidAmerican plans two 233 MW peaking plants in 2028 and 2029, and GEM has both Orient units in 2028. MidAmerican's Resource Evaluation Study of November 1, 2024 does list one 233 MW turbine in 2028 and another in 2029. Its Action Plan table says the same, with a feasible timeline of 233 MW in each of those two years. A later MidAmerican news release says the Orient Energy Center, two gas-fired combustion turbines at one site in Adair County, will generate 465 MW beginning in 2028. The company gives no 2029 date for the second turbine in that release. A queue entry at the Midcontinent Independent System Operator for 263 MW at the Orient Energy Center substation, with service in November 2028, was withdrawn on December 23, 2025. A second entry for 263 MW at the Orient to Northboro line, with service in September 2027, is still active. I did not find which entry covers which turbine. I suggest keeping 2028 for both units unless the plant's own research finds a 2029 date.

records.recommendation: Ask the reviewer to check whether Streeter Station was converted from coal to gas. If it was, add gas timepoint 2 units (16.5 MW and 35 MW) with Cedar Falls Utilities as owner.
records.researcher_notes: GEM has Streeter Station only in the coal tracker, as unit 7 (35 MW, 1973), retired. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists Streeter Station, plant 1131, owned by Cedar Falls Utilities in Black Hawk County. Both of its units are listed as natural gas steam turbines and as operating. Unit 6 is 16.5 MW from 1963. Unit 7 is 35 MW from 1973. That is 51.5 MW of gas capacity in total, which is over the 50 MW threshold. The EIA table does not say when the plants switched from coal to gas, and I did not search for the conversion date. The owner name already exists in GEM as Cedar Falls Utilities.
